direct_file_reviews.summary: The prompt requires a dependency-free Node.js ESM migration of yaml/test9.py, exact required --a parsing, PyYAML safe_load/dump behavior, .mjs files in /output, and no Python, JSON, RegExp, or npm YAML mapping shortcuts.
Parallel metadata reports actual parallel use, four subagents, artifact_ok true, process timeout, completed official evaluation, and failed solution quality of 50/146.
The completed status records swarm mode, two AgentSwarm calls, timeout, artifact files test9.mjs plus cli and yaml modules, and official evaluation failure at 50 passed of 146.
The official RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed successfully and judged the parallel artifact failing with 50 of 146 samples passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport journal for the parallel session; it contains transport/session events and provider API error records, with no projected semantic events.
Session index maps the parallel session id to the /workspace working directory and Kimi session directory.
Resolver child received the scalar resolver scope, probed PyYAML resolution, wrote /output/yaml/resolve.mjs, fixed one self-test failure, and reported passing scalar and plain-style checks.

Parser child received the YAML parser scope, probed block and flow behavior, wrote /output/yaml/parser.mjs, found four harness failures, applied partial fixes, then was resumed but did not reach a final passing report.

Dumper child received the serializer scope, wrote /output/yaml/dump.mjs, resumed after the first failed swarm, ran an end-to-end differential harness, still had 16 of 93 failures, and was cancelled before finishing.
CLI child received the argparse and entrypoint scope, wrote /output/cli/args.mjs and /output/test9.mjs, verified usage/error behavior with stubs, and completed with a handoff.

Parallel parent probed the executable, launched a four-child AgentSwarm, received two completed and two failed children, resumed parser and dumper, then the active swarm and parent turn were cancelled at timeout.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The serial prompt is byte-identical to the parallel prompt and requires the same dependency-free ESM PyYAML safe_load/dump migration with exact CLI and formatting behavior.
Serial metadata reports no parallel use, zero subagents, artifact_ok false, process timeout, completed official evaluation, and failed solution quality of 0/146.
The completed status records a single-agent run that timed out, produced no artifact files, and failed the official evaluation with 0 passed of 146.
The official RepoZero Py2JS evaluator completed successfully and judged the serial output failing with 0 of 146 samples passed.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport journal for the serial session; it contains session and tool transport events and no projected semantic events.
Session index maps the serial session id to the /workspace working directory and Kimi session directory.
Serial main worked alone, spent the run probing PyYAML and argparse behavior, began another reasoning step, and was cancelled by timeout before writing deliverables.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and children recognized the core obligations: implement PyYAML safe_load plus dump with explicit_start, exact --a CLI handling, ESM .mjs modules, output under /output, and no npm, Python, JSON, or RegExp shortcuts.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent explored behavior, then split work into four component owners: scalar resolver, YAML parser, PyYAML-style dumper, and CLI/entrypoint. The parent planned to use child results and later verify the combined implementation.
parallel.implementation: The resolver and CLI children finished and reported passing focused checks. The parser child wrote parser.mjs but still had failing harness cases during partial fixes. The dumper child wrote dump.mjs but its resumed end-to-end differential still showed 16/93 failures.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contained test9.mjs, cli/args.mjs, yaml/parser.mjs, yaml/resolve.mjs, and yaml/dump.mjs. The files were present, but the unresolved parser/dumper defects were delivered without a final successful integration pass.
parallel.verification: Children used executable probes and scratch tests. The strongest integrated evidence was negative: the resumed dumper ran node /output/test9.mjs against the executable and reported 16/93 byte-for-byte failures before cancellation; the official evaluator later passed 50/146.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Parser and dumper work did not converge before timeout, the parent never completed the planned final verifier/integration pass, and the official evaluation failed despite a nonempty artifact.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same Py2JS migration requirements and probed PyYAML output shape, scalar resolution, block scalars, anchors, key sorting, and argparse behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial run kept all work with the main agent. It did a long behavior-analysis phase and appears to have intended to start coding afterward, but no subagent or separate implementation owner existed by design.
serial.implementation: No implementation files were written to the final artifact. The only concrete actions were environment checks and executable probes, plus creation of a temporary probe helper under /workspace.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The official artifact validation found an empty artifact directory and no test9.mjs, so no integration or deliverable placement occurred.
serial.verification: The serial run verified many observed PyYAML behaviors with the executable but never verified a JavaScript implementation because no implementation was produced.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run was cancelled by timeout during reasoning/probing, with all required output files missing and official evaluation at 0/146.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM, manual CLI, zero-dependency, no Python/JSON/RegExp, and exact PyYAML output constraints and propagated them into child scopes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and analyzed the same prompt and also probed PyYAML semantics extensively.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The requirement understanding was similar; the concrete difference was that parallel converted requirements into delegated implementation files, while serial never left the probing phase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed the task into resolver, parser, dumper, and CLI/entrypoint child owners, each with file ownership under /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a single main-agent plan and execution stream without delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had component owners and concurrent progress, whereas serial retained all ownership locally and made no deliverable before cancellation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified module paths and exports such as resolveScalar, isPlainSafe, safeLoad, dumpDocument, parseArgs, and test9.mjs imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need cross-agent interface transfer; all facts remained in one main-agent context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete missing interface contract was found in parallel; the interface plan was explicit, and the failure came from unfinished parser/dumper work rather than incompatible handoffs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote resolver, parser, dumper, CLI parser, and entrypoint modules in /output through separate children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probed behavior but did not write any final implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a partial implementation that could run enough cases for 50/146, while serial delivered no executable artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first swarm returned two completed and two failed children; the parent resumed parser and dumper, but the resumed swarm ended failed/aborted as the parent turn was cancelled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to join and simply reached cancellation in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child result lifecycle with mixed results and a failed resumed batch; serial had no join problem because no parallel work existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a coherent file set in the artifact directory, with the entrypoint importing the sibling modules; no concrete same-file or overwrite collision was visible.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced no final artifact files, so there was no integration surface to assemble or collide.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had real integrated files but with unresolved behavior defects; serial had no delivered workspace state at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children performed focused probes and tests, but the resumed dumper's end-to-end differential still reported 16/93 failures before cancellation; official evaluation later failed 50/146.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed many executable probes but never had a JavaScript candidate to verify; official evaluation failed 0/146.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had implementation-level and official feedback on a partial candidate, while serial only gathered oracle behavior and had no candidate for evaluator-aligned verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent the budget on initial exploration, a four-child swarm, and a resumed parser/dumper swarm; the run timed out before final closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but its budget was consumed by a single-agent analysis and probing sequence rather than child fan-out or retries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but parallel's timeout occurred after partial artifact creation and an unfinished swarm retry, while serial timed out before producing any artifact.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed-cell outcome is both_fail: parallel failed with 50/146, serial failed with 0/146. The concrete task-solving difference is not a pass/fail discordance but artifact delivery. Parallel's swarm generated a runnable module set, yet left parser and dumper defects unresolved after a failed/resumed child cycle. Serial spent its entire turn on behavior discovery and was cancelled without any artifact files, so it received zero passing samples.
parallel_contributors: Component delegation produced resolver, parser, dumper, CLI, and entrypoint files in the artifact.
The parser/dumper retry cycle consumed the remaining time and left known differential failures unresolved.
serial_contributors: The serial agent spent the whole budget on executable probes and reasoning.
The serial artifact directory was empty at evaluation time.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel's remaining failures included unresolved serializer and parser behavior differences surfaced by its own differential harness.
Serial had no implementation defects to compare because no deliverable implementation was produced.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors for two failed runs, not an exclusive root cause

Parallel performed some initial probes, but productive module implementation was delegated after that rather than blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight.

The indispensable parser/dumper path had assigned owners; the more specific observed boundary is collective swarm and retry budget exhaustion.

candidates.near_match_reason: The active cancellation is visible, but it is treated as the downstream terminal symptom of the same fan-out retry budget episode, not an independent timing error.

candidates.reason: A dumper child cancellation is visible, but it belongs to the retained fan-out retry budget chain and does not receive a second label.
No complete, directly promotable parser/dumper candidate or mutually compatible component set existed before closure; known differential failures remained.
The observed integrated differential occurred after module files existed and reported failures; there was no later child change merged after a passing verification step.
Completed resolver and CLI implementations were present in the artifact; parser and dumper did not produce completed retrievable results that the parent ignored.
No separate verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the visible 16/93 finding was in the dumper child and part of the retained budget episode.
After the first failed parser/dumper result, the parent did attempt a resume; the later lack of takeover is downstream of the timeout in the retained fan-out budget episode.
The parent used the first swarm result to identify failed parser and dumper children and resume them; completed resolver and CLI outputs were not simply ignored.
The parent was inside AgentSwarm calls, and the observed issue is the breadth/retry budget use, not failure to inspect an available completed result during an idle wait.
Children wrote separate assigned modules with named import contracts; no competing implementation path claimed the same behavior in incompatible files.
No two live agents were shown editing the same source or configuration file and reconciling a concurrent same-file change.
No agent replaced, deleted, recreated, or wholesale rewrote a non-entry source file owned by another live agent.
The entrypoint was owned by the CLI child, and no other live actor is evidenced replacing that required deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree work.
Although children wrote to shared /output, their file ownership was separated and no unstable-state or provenance problem beyond unfinished work was observed.
No generated temp file, cache, fixture, tool, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as a false reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel parent used a broad four-child fan-out and then a failed-child resume that exhausted the run budget before parser and dumper convergence or final integrated verification.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The resumed parser/dumper work ended failed or aborted with known differential failures, leaving no final correction or acceptance pass before the timed-out artifact was evaluated.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The active child cancellation is real but is downstream of the repeated fan-out retry budget exhaustion, so it is not retained as a separate lifecycle label.
